name: OPSD-data-lite
description: Selects a teachable subset of a fixed On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) training pool and spends a short update budget on that subset rather than the whole set. The student samples on-policy answers from the problem alone; a frozen self-teacher, initialized from the same weights and conditioned on privileged context such as a reference solution, provides dense token-level supervision on those trajectories. A selector scores each candidate for sample-level teachability -- whether the privileged teacher targets a gap the question-only student can still internalize -- ranks the pool, trains on the selected subset with the standard OPSD objective, re-scores the same pool after the short round, and uses the before/after comparison to construct the next subset. Problems, privileged context, the OPSD objective, and the raw 9,600-example candidate pool stay fixed; teacher weights stay frozen at the initial student weights for a training run.
feedback_signal: Sample-level teachability over a fixed 9,600-example candidate pool. A useful example is one where the question-only student is uncertain or wrong while the privileged teacher still produces a transferable, internalizable signal; examples the student already solves, or whose teacher depends on context unavailable at inference, are treated as low value. Initial selection ranks the pool by this signal and trains on a smaller subset (2,400 examples in the reported first iteration). After a short OPSD round the same pool is re-scored; the per-sample before/after comparison filters the next subset (1,600 examples in the reported second iteration). A later aggressive pass continues the same filter down to 32 examples. Every reported data-lite iteration trains for 100 optimizer steps. The exact scoring and filter rule are withheld until publication. Benchmark outcomes are not used to choose subsets or checkpoints.
stopping_rule: No convergence or early-stopping criterion. Every data-lite iteration uses a fixed 100-step OPSD budget; only the selected subset changes: 2,400 examples, then 1,600, then an aggressive 32-example setting. Each data-lite row is compared against the 100-step full-pool OPSD control. Approximate two-cycle cost on four GPUs is 8-14 GPU-hours, dominated by full-pool scoring rather than the OPSD updates.
